Judge Rochon ordered the Trump administration to pull its multimillion-dollar ad vibe no
later than Sunday night. The ruling came after a coalition, including the nonprofit Common
Cause, challenged the taxpayer-funded Trump ads in New York federal court, arguing it
violated congressional appropriation and government propaganda rules. The White House had set
aside $20 million for the taxpayer-funded Trump ads' court record show. The campaign-styled
ads began airing in September, sparking bipartisan concern. Trump himself acknowledged the backlash
in early October, saying he'd pay for the ads himself. Despite this, the commercials,
which feature Trump and his political agenda, continued to air nationwide. The White House
did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the judge's order.
Luke Garrett, NPR News, Washington.
Three of South Carolina's candidates for U.S. Senate made their cases to voters Sunday
night in their only confirmed debate before the general election. South Carolina public
radius Luis Alfredo Garcia reports.
Republican Senator Darlene Graham and Democratic pediatrician Dr. Annie Andrews spent a good
chunk of their given debate time talking about each other. Libertarian Casey Whitener mostly
stuck to answering moderator questions, but the two leading candidates did give direct,
different answers on how the United States should navigate its policy with Israel. Graham
says the country needs to stand with its "strongest ally" in the Middle East and she condemned
Hamas. Andrews highlighted humanitarian concerns in the region.
Israelis deserve a safe place to live, and Palestinians also deserve to live in peace.
What's happening in the region is devastating. It is a humanitarian crisis.
The winner of the race will be the first woman elected to represent South Carolina in the
Senate. For NPR News, I'm Luis Alfredo Garcia in Columbia, South Carolina.
North Korea has conducted what appears to be its fourth missile launch in the past month.
NPR's Anthony Kuhn reports from Seoul that it's the first launch since October 3.
South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said the North launched multiple ballistic missiles
which traveled about 560 miles from the Pyongyang area eastward into the sea. Japan's Defense
Ministry says it also detected the launch and warned ships to watch out for falling
debris. South Korea's presidential office, known as the Blue House, held an emergency
meeting to discuss the launches, which are called illegal and urge the North to halt.
This month, both North and South Korea have tested hypersonic missiles, which are harder
to track and intercept. Last week marked the South's first hypersonic test overseen by
President E.J. Myung, while the North has conducted several such tests since 2021. Anthony
Kuhn in PR News, Seoul.
And you're listening to NPR News.
The fourth winter in Gaza since the war began is fast approaching, and humanitarian groups
say Israeli restrictions on shelter supplies are leaving Palestinians exposed to cold and
flooding. And Piers Anasbaba has a report from Gaza.
The aid group, the Norwegian Refugee Council, says 500 truckloads of shelter items are ready
to enter Gaza. But at current Israeli entry rates, it will take until next summer to bring
them in. Israel says it has facilitated the entry of tents, blankets and winter clothes.
Its military, however, says it has banned shelter kits that have wooden poles, arguing
Hamas could use them. The UN Migration Agency says nearly two million people in Gaza and
need shelter assistance, and that the agency has more than 8,500 shelter kits ready for
delivery, but that Israel's blocking these supplies at crossings. Palestinians say tents
are not a way to live, and aid groups warn a million people are at high risk of flooding.
And Asbaba, NPR News, in Gaza City.
The horror film Other Mommy topped North American box offices this weekend. The Jessica Chastain
movie earned $27.5 million in ticket sales at North American theaters. With a production
cost of $19 million, the movie is already making money. Verity dropped to second, bringing
in $11.5 million, while Resident Evil landed in third with $8.4 million. Aaron Sorkin's
The Social Reckoning had a disappointing launch, finishing fifth with just $5.5 million in
ticket sales.
